verdict.rationale: Google Authenticator documents per-code deletion, a no-account mode that keeps codes off Google's cloud, and removing synced codes by removing a device from the Google Account; a community report adds that logging out stops sync. There are no documented retention policies or controls over how long Google keeps cloud-synced copies. Community complaints about upgrades wiping data describe bugs, not a contradiction of these deletion controls. missing for 10: documented retention periods or retention settings, explicit purge of server-side synced copies, independent hands-on confirmation of deletion behavior.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: To delete an Authenticator code on Android, swipe right on any code to show the delete option.
When you first open the app, tap Use without an account.
If your codes are synced to your Google Account, you can remove codes by [removing the device from your Google Account]
you can just log out in the app to stop the synchronization
